sentences.text:
Appearance:
 Shri Ramesh Prasad Gupta - Advocate for the appellants  Shri Rajesh Gupta- Advocate for respondent No.3.
 ORDER
Heard on IA No. 4035/2019, an application under Section 5 of the Limitation Act.
2. For the reasons stated in the application, same is allowed and delay in filing instant misc. appeal is hereby condoned.

3. This appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been filed by the appellants-claimants challenging the award dated 12.02.2019 passed by the Seventh Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Gwalior (M.P.), in Claim Case No. 167/2016, seeking enhancement of compensation amount.
4. The date of the accident, the finding of negligence, and the liability are not in dispute.
The findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal on these aspects have attained finality, as the same have not been challenged in the present appeal.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:10615 2 MA-3471-2019 5.

As per the impugned award, the Claims Tribunal has awarded a total compensation of Rs.
51,66,304/- along with interest from the date of filing of the claim petition till its realization on account of the death of Vipin Kumar in the motor accident.

Smt. Sarita vs Jitendra Singh on 31 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99959558/
1 6.
Learned counsel for the appellants submits that the learned Claims Tribunal failed to appreciate the law and awarded inadequate compensation.
It is contended that appellant No.3, being the father and a dependent of the deceased, was wrongly denied compensation.

The Tribunal further erred in awarding consortium only to appellant No.1 and not to appellant Nos.2 and 3 under the head of parental consortium in the light of the judgment passed by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of United India Insurance Company Ltd.
vs. Satinder Kaur and Others reported in 2020 ACJ 2131.

entities.text:
United India Insurance Company Ltd.
vs. Satinder Kaur and Others reported in 2020 ACJ 2131
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, it is prayed that reasonable amount of compensation may be awarded to the claimants.
7. On the other hand, learned counsel for Insurance Company supported the impugned award and prayed for dismissal of appeal.

8. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the entire record of the Claims Tribunal.
9.
After hearing learned counsel for the parties and upon perusal of the record, this Court finds force in the submissions advanced on behalf of the appellants.

In view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in United India Insurance Company Ltd. (supra), the parents of the deceased are also entitled to compensation under the head of parental consortium.

The learned Claims Tribunal committed an error in not awarding consortium to NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-GWL:10615 3 MA-3471-2019 appellant Nos.2 and 3.
10.
Accordingly, the misc. appeal is allowed in part.
The appellants No.2 and 3 are held entitled to an additional amount of Rs.80,000/- (Rs.40,000/- each) towards consortium in favour of the parents of the deceased.
Except for the aforesaid modification, the rest of the award shall remain intact.
11. The miscellaneous appeal is accordingly disposed of.

(HIRDESH) JUDGE *AVI*
